_comment: IC class registry — runners (phase2/aid_class_rtl_gen/etc.) consult this to dispatch deterministic generators per detected IC class. Third-party plugins can append entries to extend coverage.

classes.name: aid_class_half_duplex_single_wire
classes.class_tree_node_basis: Every element of the registry definition is an element of the node: a cable-side device that identifies to a host over a single wire, with host-emitted framed opcodes and a CRC-8. The node sits under protocol-ic (SERIAL FRAMED), which this class satisfies, and the node's template already admits this class's CRC-8 polynomial in L3_crc_poly_allowed. 0 corpus doc-sets carry it, so the mapping is a definition, not a measured claim.
classes.description: Apple-Lightning-style half-duplex single-wire ID / authentication IC. Host emits BR + opcode (1-byte LSB-first) + optional payload; chip replies with response opcode + payload + CRC8 (poly 0x31 reflected, init 0xFF, residue 0).

classes.name: digital_cmd_driven
classes.class_tree_node_basis: The definition spans UART / SPI / I2C AND PARALLEL command interfaces. protocol-ic is defined as a SERIAL FRAMED protocol and explicitly excludes memory-mapped peripherals, so it over-claims for the parallel members; apb-peripheral over-claims for the serial ones. digital-ic is their common ancestor and the most specific node true of EVERY member. Measured on the 7 corpus doc-sets: protocol-ic would add 45 findings and digital-ic removes 11, and not one of the 45 is a defect.
classes.description: Generic command-driven digital IC (UART / SPI / I2C / parallel cmd). RTL gen not yet covered by deterministic generator — defer to spec-to-rtl skill.

classes.name: mixed_signal_otp
classes.class_tree_node_basis: analog_applicable plus a digital OTP-read control path is precisely the node's 'has analog front end' plus a digital side. The node exists but is childless AND template-less, so this mapping is INERT: a template-less node falls back to generic-ic in phase1_quality_parity_check and to any-ic in layer_extension_presence_check, measurably identical to not mapping at all.
classes.description: Mixed-signal IC with OTP-driven configuration. Digital control logic + OTP read sequence — partial overlap with aid_class. v1.6.142 (#52) routes through MAIN_FSM_SPEC_COMPLIANT so the dispatcher consumes L3.opcodes (per-opcode case-arms + L3-enumerated silent-reject arms); BASELINE spam-responder produces silent DUT for chips with opcodes outside the AID-convention default reply path.

classes.name: pure_analog
classes.class_tree_node_basis: The tree has no pure-analog node. analog-mixed-ic is the nearest, and it asserts a digital side that this class explicitly denies ('no digital RTL'). Every floor the tree can express counts a digital artefact — submodules, top-level ports, register maps — so applying any of them to a chip with no RTL is a category error rather than a strict standard. 5 corpus doc-sets; leaving it unmapped keeps their 8 findings unchanged instead of asserting something false.
classes.description: Pure analog IC — no digital RTL. Phase 2 SKIPs RTL gen; analog flow (A1..A8) handles via /vibe-ic-analog.

classes.name: data_converter
classes.class_tree_node_basis: An analog conversion core with a digital serial-readout datapath is exactly 'has analog front end' plus digital, i.e. analog-mixed-ic. The orphan template analog-front-end.yaml describes this class well but is NOT a node in the tree, so it cannot be reached by name; see the template-hole inventory. Mapping is inert until analog-mixed-ic has a template.
classes.description: ORGANIC #613 — data converter / mixed-signal IC with a digital serial readout: an analog→digital (or digital→analog) conversion core (sigma-delta / SAR / pipeline ADC, or DAC) that emits/consumes a digital serial bitstream. Has analog content AND a digital decimation / serial-readout datapath, but no SW-visible command protocol and no control FSM, so it must NOT collapse to pure_analog (which SKIPs RTL entirely). The analog track (A1..A8) sizes the converter; spec-to-rtl authors the digital decimation / serial-readout datapath; the digital backend (synth → PnR → GDS) implements it.

classes.name: bare_fpga
classes.class_tree_node_basis: The tree is rooted at any-ic, 'every IC that enters Phase 1', and this class is defined by having NO silicon target at all (Phase 3 SKIPs). No node expresses that, and adding an empty one would add exactly the template-less no-op this issue is about: a node that resolves, reads as success, and changes nothing. Recorded as unmappable until either a populated fpga-target node or an explicit no-silicon axis is warranted by a real member; the corpus has 0.
classes.description: FPGA-only design with no silicon target. Phase 2 runs FPGA-side (RTL → SOF), Phase 3 SKIPs.

classes.name: bus_interconnect_protocol
classes.class_tree_node_basis: This is a SPECIFICATION-DOCUMENT class, not an IC class — the registry entry says so ('the spec defines wire-level protocol, not an end IC', and L4/L5/L6/L10/L11/L12/L13 legitimately N/A). class-tree.yaml models ICs. bus-controller names the right subject matter but is an implementation node whose floor demands the very layers this class declares N/A, so the mapping would score a document against a chip's floor.
classes.description: v0.1.62 — for AMBA AXI/AHB/APB/ACE, Wishbone, TileLink, CHI, OCP, AvalonMM, STBus, and any other multi-channel master/slave bus-interconnect protocol SPEC document. Distinguished by valid/ready (or req/ack) handshake on per-direction channels with burst transfers and explicit master/slave (or manager/subordinate) roles. NO SW-visible opcode/command protocol — payload is data, not instructions; protocol behaviour is in channel-handshake rules. L4 (regmap), L5 (analog), L6 (FSM), L10 (test cases), L11 (OTP), L12 (calibration), L13 (lab) legitimately N/A — the spec defines wire-level protocol, not an end IC. L14-L18 (versioning, encoding tables, compliance rules, channel catalog, interconnect rules) are the SUBSTANTIVE content. Phase 2 runner dispatches via fallback_skill=spec-to-rtl when ingesting a spec for a protocol IP (e.g. an AXI master adapter); for the spec document itself, Phase 2 is N/A.

classes.name: serial_peripheral_protocol
classes.class_tree_node_basis: Also a SPECIFICATION-DOCUMENT class ('for SPI / I2C / UART / I2S / 1-Wire / CAN / SMBus / Microwire ... SPEC documents'), and additionally it spans several protocols at once, so no single leaf covers it: the natural leaves spi-peripheral and i2c-peripheral are template-less anyway. Measured on the 7 corpus doc-sets, protocol-ic would add 52 findings, none a defect.
classes.description: v0.1.77 — for SPI / I2C / UART / I2S / 1-Wire / CAN / SMBus / Microwire and similar synchronous-or-asynchronous serial peripheral SPEC documents. Distinguished by a small fixed external pin count (typically 2-4) carrying named functions (data/clock/select), master/slave (or controller/target) roles, a shift register as the core data-movement primitive, and clock-divisor / baud-rate control. No multi-channel handshake (that's bus_interconnect_protocol) and no SW-visible opcode protocol (that's digital_cmd_driven). L4 register map IS present (configuration register file at the host-bus interface); L5 (analog), L11 (OTP), L13 (lab cal) typically N/A. L14-L18 (versioning, encoding tables, compliance rules, channel catalog, interconnect rules) all apply to the serial protocol layer. Phase 2 runner dispatches via fallback_skill=spec-to-rtl since the spec is a wire-level protocol, not a complete IC.

classes.name: digital_arithmetic_primitive
classes.class_tree_node_basis: This name does two jobs and only one of them is a class. ic_class_profile uses it as the TERMINAL CATCH-ALL: all 11 corpus doc-sets carrying it record decisive_evidence 'L1/L2 present + no analog + no cmd protocol + no protocol/cpu signature -> arithmetic-primitive catch-all', i.e. they are UNCLASSIFIED, not classified as arithmetic. A floor hung here would score the classifier's uncertainty as the design's deficiency. digital-ic asserts only what that branch actually established (no analog, digital). If and when the catch-all is split from the real datapath class, the real one belongs at dsp-block; until then that mapping would cost 22 findings and crypto-engine 75, on 11 doc-sets nobody classified.
classes.description: v1.6.522 — for #358 P2. Pure digital data-transform IP (multiplier, adder, filter, hash core, encoder/decoder, arithmetic sub-block). No SW-visible protocol / register map / calibration. Single top module with clock + reset + data ports. L4/L5/L6 legitimately N/A — L2 describes a deterministic combinational/sequential data transform. Phase 2 runner dispatches via fallback_skill=spec-to-rtl since there is no deterministic RTL generator for this open family.

classes.name: processor_cpu
classes.class_tree_node_basis: 'Instruction-fetch, load/store, register file' against the node's 'instruction-fetching, register-file, pipelined compute core' is an exact match. The registry entry also says 'or SoC', which soc-harness covers better, but the dominant and defining reading is the core.
classes.description: v1.6.523 — CPU / processor core / SoC with a memory-bus / data top (instruction-fetch, load/store, register file). No SW-visible half-duplex command protocol on a single-wire bus and no analog content. The AID 3-port (clk/reset_n/id_bus) reference TB cannot bind a memory-bus top, so Phase 2 verification runs the generic full-stack TB driven from L9.top_ports + gate-level synth + Phase 3 instead. RTL gen via fallback_skill / IP-catalog glue (open-source RISC-V / SoC cores).

classes.name: bus_peripheral
classes.class_tree_node_basis: The registry class is a register-mapped peripheral behind a bus subordinate port; the node is 'memory-mapped, NOT a serial protocol' with a register window. The node names APB while the class also spans TL-UL / AXI-Lite / AHB / Wishbone, but the bus flavour is incidental to every floor the node carries (all of them count register-map and integration content, none of them count APB signalling), and the registry's own synonyms include apb_peripheral.
classes.description: ORGANIC #542 — Register-mapped peripheral IP: SW-visible register map (hjson/regmap or equivalent) exposed via a bus subordinate interface (TL-UL, APB, AXI-Lite, Wishbone, AHB). No ISA / instruction-fetch semantics. L4 register map is the primary specification layer. Distinguished from bus_interconnect_protocol (wire-level protocol spec) and processor_cpu (instruction-executing). crypto_accelerator takes priority when crypto algorithm features are present. ORGANIC #677 — a MINIMAL instance (e.g. a Wishbone-mapped counter with no regmap / no test scenarios / no test cases) may honestly declare the absence via no_register_map_in_input / no_test_scenarios_in_input / no_test_cases_in_input == true; minimal_honest_absence_ok lets l_doc_structured_field_count_check waive the L4/L7/L10 typed-field floors for that honest minimal doc (NARROWER than command_protocol_applicable so a reused-IP processor_cpu still obeys its #641 populated-bring-up doctrine).

classes.name: crypto_accelerator
classes.class_tree_node_basis: 'Algorithm data-path plus a SW-accessible register interface, no external protocol' against 'self-contained crypto block (no external protocol; register IO)' is an exact match.
classes.description: ORGANIC #542 — Cryptographic accelerator IP: hardware implementation of AES, SHA, HMAC, ECC, ChaCha or similar. Typically pairs an algorithm data-path with a SW-accessible register interface for key loading, control, and status. Distinguishable by algorithm-domain vocabulary (encrypt/decrypt, key schedule, S-box, digest, IV/nonce) plus register-map features. Takes priority over bus_peripheral when crypto algorithm evidence is present.

classes.name: unknown_protocol_class
classes.class_tree_node_basis: The entry means 'detection failed', which is the same category as the digital_arithmetic_primitive catch-all: there is nothing to score. any-ic is the honest node — it asserts only that the thing entered Phase 1. Note this is deliberately WEAKER than today's behaviour, where an unresolvable class falls back to the generic-ic floor in phase1_quality_parity_check; a failed classification must not be graded.
classes.description: Detection failed or class not yet registered. Runner fall-throughs to fallback_skill — AI takes over via /spec-to-rtl skill.
